guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 34
A MAJOR PENTATONIC FIVE-POSITION CONNECTION - FIXED-KEY NECK MAP
PURPOSE
Stop transposing one shape. Keep the key fixed as A major pentatonic and move through five common
positions from the low-E root frame at frets 4-7 through the octave frame at frets 14-17. Learn each
vertical position, connect adjacent positions around one shared anchor note on every string, then link
all five frames in a forward and reverse zigzag.
IMPORTANT POSITION-LABEL NOTE
Pentatonic box numbers vary among methods. This workbook numbers positions in ascending-neck order,
beginning with the A-root frame around low-E fret 5. Use the fret spans, degree maps, and root locations
as the authoritative identity of each position.
A MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Notes: A B C# E F#
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
POSITION SUMMARY
P1 ROOT FRAME             frets 4-7    starts degree 1  roots E5, D7, e5
Ascending degrees: 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2
P2 SECOND-DEGREE FRAME    frets 6-10   starts degree 2  roots D7, B10
Ascending degrees: 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3
P3 THIRD-DEGREE FRAME     frets 9-12   starts degree 3  roots A12, B10
Ascending degrees: 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5
P4 FIFTH-DEGREE FRAME     frets 11-14  starts degree 5  roots A12, G14
Ascending degrees: 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6
P5 SIXTH-DEGREE FRAME     frets 14-17  starts degree 6  roots E17, G14, e17
Ascending degrees: 6 1 2 3 5 6 1 2 3 5 6 1
PICKING AND COUNTS
Each vertical position cell contains 24 notes: 12 ascending and 12 descending with the high endpoint repeated.
Each shared-anchor seam cell contains 30 notes: six five-note string groups. Every five-note group flips the
starting stroke on the next string, but the complete 30-note cell is even.
The forward zigzag contains 60 notes; the reverse zigzag contains 60 notes. Repeat high-e fret 17 at the
turn when linking them, producing an even 120-note circuit.
Five position cells = 120 notes. Four seam cells = 120 notes. Linked zigzag = 120 notes.
Complete Level 34 workout = 360 notes.
STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string crossing, shared anchor, position
boundary, root, outer-string turn, or the forward/reverse turnaround.
FIVE VERTICAL POSITION CELLS

semantic_guidance.forward_route_text:
Route: P1 ASC -> high-e 7 to 9 -> P2 DESC -> low-E 7 to 9 -> P3 ASC -> high-e 12 to 14 ->
       P4 DESC -> low-E 12 to 14 -> P5 ASC.
Every position segment contains 12 notes, so every new frame begins with the same pick orientation.

semantic_guidance.practice_mastery_text:
PRACTICE PROGRESSION
========================================================================================================================
1. Map P1-P5 and say each starting degree.
2. Play every 24-note vertical cell with both pick starts.
3. Learn all four 30-note shared-anchor seam cells.
4. Play the 60-note forward zigzag without a seam pause.
5. Play the 60-note reverse zigzag without a seam pause.
6. Link forward and reverse as one 120-note circuit.
7. Accent every A root, then remove the accents while continuing to hear A as tonic.

ERROR DIAGNOSIS
LOST KEY CENTER: Stop on the nearest A root, sing A, and restart the local frame.
WRONG BOX: Name the position span and its first low-E degree before playing.
EARLY SHIFT: Remain in the lower frame through the shared anchor; move only after it sounds.
NOISY SEAM: Release pressure, move the thumb with the hand, and reduce the tempo by 4-6 BPM.
PICK RESET: Mute the strings and air-pick the exact 12-, 30-, or 60-note count.
TENSION: Stop, shake out, and practice one seam instead of forcing the full route.

ADVANCEMENT RULES
Add 2 BPM after three clean circuits at the current route length.
After two errors, reduce 4-6 BPM or shorten the route to one adjacent-position seam.
Increase route length before speed when the shift is weak. Increase speed before route length when the map is secure.

MASTERY GATE BEFORE LEVEL 35
Name all five positions and fret spans; play each vertical cell with D-start and U-start; shift at every
shared anchor without a scrape or hesitation; complete the linked 120-note zigzag on two separate days;
identify every A root by sight and sound; and recover the correct position after a deliberate random stop.
semantic_guidance.reverse_route_text:
Route: P5 DESC -> low-E 14 to 12 -> P4 ASC -> high-e 14 to 12 -> P3 DESC -> low-E 9 to 7 ->
       P2 ASC -> high-e 9 to 7 -> P1 DESC.
When linking forward and reverse, articulate high-e fret 17 at the end of the forward route and again to
begin the reverse route. The linked circuit contains 120 notes and returns to low-E fret 5.
semantic_guidance.seam_instruction_text:
For each string, play lower outer note -> shared anchor -> upper outer note -> shared anchor -> lower outer note.
Stay in the lower-position fingering through note 2. Shift after the anchor sounds, play note 3 in the upper
frame, return to the anchor as note 4, then shift back before note 5. Do not re-articulate the anchor merely
to disguise the hand movement.

guidance_lines.text: SCALE EXERCISES - SECTION IV, LEVEL 35
A MAJOR PENTATONIC HORIZONTAL STRING LANES - CONTROLLED SHIFTS, SLIDES, AND DESTINATION LANDINGS
PURPOSE
Keep the key fixed as A major pentatonic and turn the five vertical positions from Level 34 into six
horizontal one-string melodies. First relocate silently between three two-note stations, then isolate one
timed slide at each of the four position seams, then land directly on named destinations over increasing
distances. Finish by linking all six strings in a forward and reverse horizontal snake.
IMPORTANT INTERPRETATION
This level does not transpose the shape. Every note belongs to A major pentatonic: A B C# E F#.
The suggested route fingerings are designed for continuous one-string movement and therefore do not always
match the vertical-box fingerings from Level 34. The fret, note, degree, and timing are authoritative.
A MAJOR-PENTATONIC FORMULA
Degrees: 1 2 3 5 6
Notes:   A B C# E F#
Intervals: whole - whole - minor third - whole - minor third
HORIZONTAL LANE SUMMARY
Low E   frets 5 7 9 12 14 17     degrees 1 2 3 5 6 1  notes A B C# E F# A    fingers 1 3 1 4 1 4 roots 5,17
A       frets 4 7 9 12 14 16     degrees 3 5 6 1 2 3  notes C# E F# A B C#   fingers 1 4 1 4 1 3 roots 12
D       frets 4 7 9 11 14 16     degrees 6 1 2 3 5 6  notes F# A B C# E F#   fingers 1 4 1 3 1 3 roots 7
G       frets 4 6 9 11 14 16     degrees 2 3 5 6 1 2  notes B C# E F# A B    fingers 1 3 1 3 1 3 roots 14
B       frets 5 7 10 12 14 17    degrees 5 6 1 2 3 5  notes E F# A B C# E    fingers 1 3 1 3 1 4 roots 10
High e  frets 5 7 9 12 14 17     degrees 1 2 3 5 6 1  notes A B C# E F# A    fingers 1 3 1 4 1 4 roots 5,17
PICKING AND COUNT RULES
Module A: six 12-note picked cells = 72 picked notes.
Module B: 24 slide phrases x 6 sounding tones = 144 sounding tones, but only 96 pick attacks.
Module C: six 16-note destination ladders = 96 picked notes.
Module D: forward 36 + reverse 36 = 72 picked notes.
Complete Level 35 workout = 384 sounding tones / 336 pick attacks.
STRICT ALTERNATE PICKING
Complete separate D-start and U-start passes. Do not restart at a string change, station shift, seam slide,
repeated destination, A root, or forward/reverse turnaround. A slide destination is sounded without a new
pick attack and must arrive exactly on the subdivision.
MODULE A - SIX SILENT-SHIFT HORIZONTAL LANES
Group each lane into three two-note stations. Use finger 1-3 for a whole step and 1-4 for a minor third.
Shift after the first station and after the second station. Release pressure before moving. No slide is allowed.

semantic_guidance.module_a:
MODULE A - SIX SILENT-SHIFT HORIZONTAL LANES
========================================================================================================================
Group each lane into three two-note stations. Use finger 1-3 for a whole step and 1-4 for a minor third.
Shift after the first station and after the second station. Release pressure before moving. No slide is allowed.
semantic_guidance.module_b:
========================================================================================================================
For every string: pick the lower note; pick the shared anchor and slide to the upper destination; re-pick the
destination and slide back to the anchor; pick the lower note. Each phrase contains 6 sounding tones but
only 4 pick attacks. Use finger 3 for a two-fret slide and finger 4 for a three-fret slide.
semantic_guidance.module_c:
========================================================================================================================
Launch from the lower endpoint of each string. Land on the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth lane notes in turn.
Each four-note cell is launch -> target -> repeated target -> launch. First pass: use finger 1 on every note.
No slide is allowed. After the printed pass, begin at the upper endpoint and mirror the target order downward.
semantic_guidance.module_d:
========================================================================================================================
Every segment contains six notes. Because six is even, each new string begins with the original pick-start
orientation. Do not reset at a string change.

FORWARD ROUTE: Low E ASC -> A DESC -> D ASC -> G DESC -> B ASC -> High e DESC
Transitions: E17/A16 | A4/D4 | D16/G16 | G4/B5 | B17/e17
